result.summary: The image shows a standard urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks, sidewalks, and a traffic signal. While basic infrastructure is present, the environment lacks advanced safety features like curb extensions or dedicated pedestrian signals, and parked vehicles near the crossing may limit visibility.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk on both sides of the street can obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs adjacent to the crosswalk markings

hazards.name: Lack of Dedicated Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks, sidewalks, and signalized control. However, the crossing distance is relatively wide without a median refuge, and parked vehicles near the corners may obstruct sight lines.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines for both pedestrians and motorists.
